sources.title: Dynamic workflows
findings: Public preview, available in Copilot app, CLI, and SDK, subject to billing-plan eligibility.
Workflow code defines steps, conditions, handoffs, and when agents are involved.
Autopilot controls autonomy; fleet lets the model decompose work; a dynamic workflow defines a reusable process in code.
Extension code can run outside subagent permission prompts.
AI-credit limits are approximate post-paid limits, not hard ceilings.

sources.title: Using dynamic workflows
findings: CLI requires experimental features.
Project definitions are extension.mjs files beneath .github/extensions.
Run by name from a prompt or with copilot workflow run.
The /workflows command and app Workflows panel expose progress and resume.
App run monitoring is available only for local sessions.
Copying an extension shares its definition, not its history or saved run state.

sources.title: Official SDK: Dynamic Workflows
findings: defineWorkflow and joinSession register an extension workflow.
ctx.agent supports schema, model, reasoningEffort, agent, contextTier, and label.
Ordinary agent failures return null; cancellation and hard runtime failures reject.
ctx.step journals by key alone; producers must return JSON and should be idempotent.
ctx.pause creates a durable one-shot checkpoint; resume restarts the body using saved steps.
Structured output validates a subset of JSON Schema; numeric ranges and additionalProperties are not enforced.
Identical prompt/options calls are memoized; unique labels distinguish independent agents.
Nested workflows are not supported.

sources.title: Official SDK: Copilot CLI Extensions
findings: Extensions run in separate Node.js processes over JSON-RPC stdio.
Copilot injects @github/copilot-sdk; project users need not install the SDK for the extension.
Sensitive environment variables are stripped unless explicitly requested and approved.

sources.title: CLI programmatic reference
findings: Direct workflow runs do not show permission prompts; configure required permissions beforehand.
GITHUB_COPILOT_PROMPT_MODE_EXTENSIONS=true opts into running trusted project extension code for that invocation.
Only successful runs with a result update --result-file; stale result files can survive failed runs.
Paused runs use exit code 1, completed runs 0, and unknown workflows or invalid arguments 2.

sources.title: Running tasks in parallel with /fleet
findings: The main agent decides decomposition and coordinates dependencies.
Independent subtasks may run in parallel, each with a separate context window.
Fleet may increase AI-credit use and offers no inherent benefit for sequential work.

sources.title: Allowing Copilot CLI to work autonomously
findings: Autopilot continues through successive steps until complete, blocked, interrupted, or limited.
Autonomy is distinct from tool/path/URL permissions.
Wide permission grants require care and are not a substitute for a sandbox.

sources.title: Working with agent sessions in the Copilot app
findings: The app supports parallel sessions, worktree/local/cloud locations, modes, models, and reasoning effort.
Isolation depends on the chosen execution location; a folder/local session is not an isolated worktree.
The app is built on Copilot CLI.

sources.title: Creating and using custom agents for CLI
findings: Custom profiles use .agent.md files in .github/agents or the personal agents directory.
CLI personal profiles take precedence over same-ID repository profiles.
Subagents do not follow repository custom instructions by default; include-custom-instructions is opt-in.

sources.title: Custom agents configuration
findings: Tools can be restricted; tools: [] disables all tools.
Model availability and environment-specific profile behavior must be checked in the actual client.
The CLI-specific precedence documented in S9 should not be replaced with cloud-agent precedence rules.

sources.title: Using automations in the Copilot app
findings: Local and cloud automations support recurring or on-demand agent tasks.
Cloud automation requires applicable repository and organization policies.
Saving a trigger is not the same as authoring a dynamic workflow.

sources.title: Repository configuration for the Copilot app
findings: .github/github-app.yml controls project instructions, scripts, server detection, and automation behavior.
Repository configuration must be reviewed and trusted before it applies.
App scripts receive credentials; never log or persist their environment.

sources.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows: About
findings: gh-aw is a separate open-source GitHub CLI extension for AI-powered automation on GitHub Actions.
Markdown with YAML frontmatter compiles to a .lock.yml Actions workflow.
It complements deterministic CI rather than replacing it.

sources.title: How GitHub Agentic Workflows work
findings: Actions supplies triggers, runners, logs, and job orchestration.
AI engines include Copilot, Claude, Codex, Gemini, and Pi.
Agent jobs have minimal read-only permissions by default; configured safe outputs apply writes separately.

sources.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows security architecture
findings: Defense in depth includes compilation validation, runtime isolation, permission separation, network controls, and output handling.
Controls are configurable; safe outputs do not make untrusted instructions safe by definition.
Review generated workflow permissions and require human review for consequential changes.

sources.title: GitHub Agentic Workflows safe outputs
findings: Configured operations are validated and applied by scoped jobs.
A safe output is a constrained write mechanism, not a proof of correctness.

sources.title: About agent skills
findings: Skills package task-specific instructions and optional resources.
Skills do not themselves provide the durability or runtime semantics of a dynamic workflow.

sources.title: VS Code agents overview
findings: Editor agents are another Copilot surface.
Do not promise identical CLI/app workflow APIs or monitoring UI in every editor.

sources.title: Official SDK: custom agents and sub-agent orchestration
findings: SDK sessions explicitly accept customAgents with names, prompts, scoped tools, models, and reasoning effort.
The delivered SDK host loads the repository prompts into explicit tools: [] profiles.
Runtime model resolution is checked before a proposal is accepted; fallback is not allowed.

sources.title: Official SDK: workflow end-to-end tests
findings: Standalone SDK extension hosting needs an explicit extension launch provider and SDK injection path.
The official bootstrap supplies SDK resolution and a parent-process lifecycle watchdog.
The delivered host restricts its launch provider to the exact project:launch-rescue entrypoint.
